vintagecanvas:basics-text: Your first steps in Vintage Canvas Welcome to Vintage Canvas! To begin your creative journey, you'll need a couple of things at minimum: an easel, any shape of canvas, and a charcoal stick. Place your easel in the world (ideally somewhere with good light). Place your canvas onto the easel using rightmousebutton. Then, hold your charcoal stick, and sketch away to your heart's content! To show off your creation, take it out of the easel with an empty hand, and put it up on any wall. For some extra flair, you can use any wooden board to frame the canvas while it's hanging up! Blending If your sketch is looking too coarse for your liking, consider crafting a brush. A brush without any paint serves as a blender, letting you create smooth gradients and lighter colours. To correct mistakes, consider making a chalk stick.
vintagecanvas:frescos-text: The simplest way to paint As an alternative to canvases, Vintage Canvas also supports fresco painting. To make a fresco, craft some fresco plaster. Apply this to a chiselled block (non-chiselled blocks are not currently supported), and use any of your painting tools to display your talents directly on the walls. Note that frescos are fragile, and can’t be picked up without being destroyed. To make portable art, you’ll need to use a canvas.
vintagecanvas:painting-text: Painting Once you're ready for a bigger challenge, it's time to create some paint! Make a couple of paint jars, fill them with some oil, and add any pigment - like crushed lapis lazuli, cinnabar, charcoal - or one of the new pigments added by Vintage Canvas. If you’re short on oil, you can create an alternate medium called ‘tempera’ by adding an egg to a paint jar full of water. Next, craft yourself one or all of the paint brushes. Right-click to dip your paint in the jar of your choice, and paint away! If you're looking for more than the flat colours of basic pigments, you have two options: paint thinning, and paint mixing. Paint Thinning To reduce the opacity of your paint, dip your brush with paint into a jar of turpentine. The more times you dip it, the more transparent the paint - ideal for making blended colours! Paint mixing Still not satisfied with the colours at your disposal? Time to craft a palette! When placed in the world, this nifty plank gives you nine slots in which to combine basic paints. Click any slot with a paint jar to add its colour to the mix. Keep adding paints until you've got your ideal tone! Right-click the slot with a brush to use the paint, same as any paint jar. To clean out a slot, right-click it with your turpentine jar. Blending You can use a fresh, paintless brush to blend colours on the canvas. To clean out a brush, crouch + right-click your brush onto a turpentine jar.
vintagecanvas:large-text: Large paintings To paint a large canvas, you need a large easel. Once you've got one set up, you can combine any two canvases into their corresponding upgraded size. You get four times the surface area for just twice the materials, so it's an excellent deal!
vintagecanvas:settings-text: By default, paint slowly gets consumed as you use brushes, palettes, and jars. If you just want to paint without interruption, you can toggle this setting off in the mod config (PaintDepletion: false). Alternatively, you can increase the amount of painting you can do with a given amount of paint.
